sylvia-ps: FYI we're kicking off a pilot with MeridianPay next week. They're wiring our SDK behind a gateway-proxy that only exposes a single HTTP/2 connection and want to multiplex many logical streams. Main asks: Python SDK mux examples, consistent spans/labels for their APM, ephemeral credential rotation for short-lived tokens, SOC2 + ISO27001 questionnaire, and a rough hosted vs dedicated cost for sudden 3k QPS spikes. Can someone put together a tiny runbook + snippets?

omar-sales: Demo requested Tue 11am ET. They start on Hosted and may request Dedicated if latency/determinism looks good. Need a concise ops note we can hand to their infra team.

lee-runtime: Notes on muxing over a single HTTP/2 connection: our runtime accepts multiplexed logical streams via stream_id header on the initial upgrade request. Python example (streaming):
```py
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('RW_KEY'), enable_mux=True)
stream = client.stream(model='gpt-4o-infer', stream_id='meridian-mail-01', trace=True)
for chunk in stream:
    print('chunk', chunk)
# start another logical stream reusing the transport
stream2 = client.stream(model='gpt-4o-infer', stream_id='meridian-mail-02')
```
If their proxy rewrites headers, set transport_hint: 'http2-proxy' so we use header-based muxing. Fallback: open separate short-lived connections per logical stream or use non-streaming / batch endpoints.

lee-runtime: Telemetry/labels: recommend these tags on every logical stream: app=meridian, env=pilot, stream_id, request_shard. We ingest these into traces when trace:true. If they use Datadog/NewRelic, include x-trace-id header to correlate.

nina-devx: For function/tool calls and structured output, suggest a tiny contract they can validate locally. Example minimal function call we demo: 
```json
{"name":"charge_card","params":{"type":"object","properties":{"card_last4":{"type":"string"},"amount":{"type":"number"}},"required":["amount"]}}
```
Also advise they run a small validation harness (5 prompts) to ensure stable parsing. We provide a standalone Node/Python validator snippet in the runbook.

secbot: For compliance: ask Meridian procurement to send vendor SOC2/ISO questionnaire PDF to security@redwood.ai. Quick blockers: (1) data flow diagram + retention policy, (2) confirmation whether raw utterances contain PII and where logs land, (3) if Dedicated requested we need KMS details + contractual SLAs. Typical turnaround: 2-4 business days after receiving questionnaire and diagrams.

omar-sales: Pricing: any quick host vs dedicate guidance for 3k QPS spikes? They called out bursts lasting ~5-8 minutes, several times per day.

lee-runtime: For that pattern we usually recommend either a small Dedicated slice sized for the peak or Hosted with negotiated burst credits. Example: a dedicated GPU slice to handle that burst might be in the $8k-15k/mo range depending on preferred GPU and quantization. Hosted burst credit pricing is handled case-by-case; for the demo offer to run a simulated 1k QPS for 5 minutes so they can see perf.

omar-sales: I'll draft a single-paragraph cost summary and optional trial reservation note.

sylvia-ps: Can someone produce a one-page runbook + two code snippets (Python mux, curl fallback) by EOD Monday? I will forward their procurement contact and the questionnaire once I have it.

nina-devx: I'll assemble the runbook and include a troubleshooting section: common mux failures (header stripping, body coalescing), token expiry 401 flows (refresh token dance), and a note about payload size influencing batching heuristics.

lee-runtime: I'll add a small script to simulate multiplexed load (python async worker) and share kernel-tuning notes (max_tokens, batch_window_ms).

secbot: Confirmed 100 will triage questionnaire once received.

omar-sales: Scheduling: quick sync Mon 4pm PT to finalize runbook and pricing slide?

sylvia-ps: Works for me. Thanks team 680 I will drop initial payload examples and their expected QPS distribution in the channel now.
